newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- JCI managing director Bill Nairn has resigned. Analysts and JCI sources said he had "agreed to stand down" after his position was compromised by having backed the wrong horse in the race for effective control of the mining house.

It was common knwoledge in the market that Nairn favoured losing bidder New Africa Investments, led by Cyril Ramaphosa, as opposed to new owners Saflife, which ended up controlling JCI after the African Mining Group failed to raise the required funds, they said.

- Laurent Kabila's Zairean rebels on Tuesday gave Patrick Claes, the managing director of Spoornet's jointly owned Zairean railway company, 24 hours to vacate his office and home and leave Lubumbashi, Spoornet said on Tuesday night.
- Housing Minister Sankie Mthembi-Mahanyele unveiled plans on Tuesday to protect consumers from unscrupulous developers by making the registration of builders using government subsidies compulsory.

- SA mining houses Gencor and Avgold intend to merge their wholly owned and contiguous gold mining operations Fairview and Eastern Transvaal Consolidated ETCJ.J (ET Cons), creating a low-cost operation in an estimated 900 million rand deal.
- Outspan, Appletiser and the Krugerrand are among the top 300 international brands, according to the latest edition of the UK publication, The World's Greatest Brands.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The resignation on Tuesday of Bill Nairn, the managing director of JCI, sent shock waves through the recently sold mining house, with analysts speculating that further reshuffles and senior-level departures were imminent.

- Retail group Edgars on Tuesday reported its first drop in full-year earnings in 10 years, with earnings for the 12 months to March 31 down seven percent to 598 cents a share from 642 cents previously.

- Primedia, the acquisition-hungry media conglomerate, is about to snap up George Warman Publications, the well-established specialist magazine and journal publisher, sources close to the deal said on Tuesday.

- The government has lured a consortium of companies, led by the international petroleum company Phillips, into signing an agreement to explore 14,5 million acres off the Kwazulu-Natal coast for oil and gas with a tax offer which may contravene the Income Tax Act.
- The expextations of world leaders in the computer industry decades ago have left modern-age computer gurus reeling with mirth, not only because of the speed at which change has taken place.
SAKE BEELD

- A Liquor Act provision allowing grocers to sell wine, but not malt or spirits, was a direct result of the then National Party government's policy to protect KWV and specifically wine producers and farmers in the Cape from competitors such as beer brewers.

- The SA Revenue Service plans to establish regional offices in all nine provinces and would be ready in about three years, two senior officials from the service told a parliamentary committee on Tuesday.
- Comprehensive changes will be made to the format and contents of the annual budget. The process will be more transparent in future and no longer shrouded in secrecy as in the past.
THE STAR
- A former Bophuthatswana policeman confessed on Tuesday to shooting dead three AWB members as they lay wounded next to their car in Mmabatho on March 11, 1994.
- The government's bid to trim the civil service has resulted in only 323 million rand being saved from voluntary severance packages -- almost 4,5 million rand less than had been projected.

- More than 10,000 arrests were made and stolen property worth over 1,7 million rand was seized in Gauteng in the past three weeks as law enforcers battle to curb the province's spiralling crime rate.
